current_determination: At quadratic order the reflection-adapted soft gauge kernel can be chosen to have exactly Bałaban's linear block average Q. Its fine-field Hessian is M+a Q^T Q, the same propagator family already used in the Gaussian/vector-field analysis. After integrating the fine field, however, fixed-a soft blocking is not identical to the hard constraint: if C=Q M^{-1}Q^T, the hard coarse Hessian is Delta_infty=C^{-1} while the soft one is Delta_a=(C+a^{-1}I)^{-1}. Their difference is -a^{-1} Delta_infty^2(I+a^{-1}Delta_infty)^{-1}, hence schematically p^4/a at low momentum when Delta_infty~p^2. The mismatch is therefore a candidate irrelevant higher-derivative operator rather than a generated mass. Fixed kappa does not become a hard constraint merely as g->0 in canonically rescaled fields; YM-R18 is corrected on that point. The remaining theorem deficit is inductive closure of this quadratic irrelevant correction plus the normalized kernel's cubic-and-higher local analytic remainder in Bałaban's polymer/effective-action norms.
major_new_results: The soft matrix kernel can be path-weighted so its linearization is exactly the Bałaban gauge averaging operator Q.
The normalized weak-field kernel has leading conditional Gaussian form (a/2)||B-QA||^2.
The soft fine-field Green operator is (M+aQ^TQ)^{-1}, exactly the Gaussian operator family already present in Bałaban-style propagator analysis.
Hard coarse Hessian: Delta_infty=(QM^{-1}Q^T)^{-1}; soft coarse Hessian: Delta_a=(QM^{-1}Q^T+a^{-1}I)^{-1}.
The soft-hard quadratic difference is higher derivative at low momentum: Delta_a-Delta_infty ~ -a^{-1}p^4 when Delta_infty~p^2.
Linear gauge covariance Qd=dQ_0 prevents the Q^TQ term from being interpreted as a physical Proca mass.
Reflection-aligned straight-path averaging is compatible with positive-half-space support away from the reflection boundary.
correction_to_prior_state: YM-R18's statement that fixed-kappa soft blocking automatically becomes the hard delta constraint as beta->infinity was coordinate-dependent and too strong. In canonically rescaled weak fields the soft width remains finite for fixed kappa/a. Exact hard recovery requires a->infinity; fixed a instead defines a distinct RG scheme whose leading difference is an irrelevant quadratic operator.
